title: Cache telemetry: add sampling controls + local rate limiting for high-volume events
author: Thomas Baird
description:
Problem: the new cache telemetry (hit/miss counters, eviction events, wasted prefill) is intentionally emitted at request boundaries and (in a few places) per-cache-event to support attribution. Under some workloads (streaming chat retries, high QPS short prompts, and continuous batching), this can become a high-volume signal source. We need guardrails so we don’t introduce p95/p99 latency overhead in runtime or create a sudden telemetry cost spike in prod.

This PR adds two layers of protection:
1) Deterministic sampling for event-style cache signals (and optionally for a subset of histograms) with stable sampling keys so ratios remain interpretable at aggregation time.
2) A lightweight local rate limiter in the runtime emitter path that caps the maximum number of cache telemetry emissions per process per interval, with self-observability metrics for drops.

What’s included (high level):
- New config surface (runtime) for cache telemetry sampling + rate limits:
  - cache_telemetry.enabled (default: on in staging, off in prod until rollout gate)
  - cache_telemetry.event_sample_rate (default: 0.05 in staging)
  - cache_telemetry.histogram_sample_rate (default: 1.0; can be reduced if needed)
  - cache_telemetry.max_events_per_second (token bucket; default: 2,000/s)
  - cache_telemetry.burst (default: 5,000)
- Deterministic sampling based on a stable key derived from request_id + route_id + model_version_id. (No prompt content is used; privacy-safe.)
- Rate limiting is applied after sampling, so we keep behavior predictable and don’t overwhelm the emitter path on pathological spikes.
- Drop counters + reason tags so SRE can tell “real hit-rate change” vs “telemetry is being throttled”:
  - redwood.cache.telemetry.dropped_total{reason=rate_limited|disabled}
  - redwood.cache.telemetry.sampled_total{signal=pfx_event|kv_event|evict_event|wasted_prefill}
- Updates to docs/comments in the runtime telemetry module to clarify which signals are sampled and how to interpret them downstream (aggregation must scale by 1/sample_rate for sampled signals).

Non-goals:
- No changes to metric definitions / ADR semantics.
- No ingestion-side cardinality policy changes (handled separately).

Testing:
- Unit tests for deterministic sampling boundaries and token bucket behavior.
- Load test in perf-canary branch (manual run linked in comments) showed no measurable regression at 5% event sampling + 2k/s cap; without cap we saw occasional emitter contention in debug builds.

Rollout plan:
- Staging: enable cache_telemetry.enabled=true + 5% sampling by default.
- Canary: enable in 1% prod traffic with max_events_per_second=500 initially; ramp after 24h if no latency regression and dropped_total remains <1% of sampled_total.

Follow-ups:
- PR-18429 will wire these flags into our environment config defaults and make them operator-tunable via the control plane; this PR keeps the knobs local to the runtime config struct + CLI/env config parsing used in tests.

Risk notes:
- Sampling changes require careful interpretation in dashboards; this PR emits explicit sampled_total/dropped_total so we can sanity check the effective sampling rate and throttling behavior before we rely on the signals for recommendations.

conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Can we ensure sampling is deterministic so dashboards don’t jitter day-to-day? Also please confirm no prompt content participates in the key.

Thomas Baird (author): Yes—sampling uses a stable 64-bit hash of (request_id, route_id, model_version_id). request_id is already a UUID generated at gateway and propagated; route/model ids are stable join keys. No prompt bytes or token content is included. I added a comment + unit test that sampling decisions are stable for a fixed key.

Nadia Rahman (review): We should emit explicit “dropped due to rate limit” counters, otherwise ingestion drops vs runtime throttling will be hard to diagnose. Also prefer reason enums that won’t churn.

Thomas Baird (author): Added redwood.cache.telemetry.dropped_total{reason=rate_limited|disabled} and kept the reason set intentionally small. Also added sampled_total by signal so we can compute the effective rate.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Why are we sampling histograms at all? Hit/miss counters are cheap but per-event emissions are the concern. I’d rather keep histograms unsampled unless we have evidence they’re hot.

Thomas Baird (author): Agree. Default histogram_sample_rate=1.0; only event-style signals are sampled by default. The knob exists as an escape hatch if we find a specific histogram is too expensive under extreme QPS.

Marcus Reed (perf review): Any evidence of overhead? Please include perf numbers or at least show we’re not adding locks on the hot path.

Thomas Baird (author): Limiter uses an atomic token bucket with a fast-path check; no mutex. I added unit tests and included results from a local perf run in tools/perf/notes/cache-telemetry-sampling.md. In release build, delta in p95 was within noise; the main win is preventing spikes under bursty cache-event emission.

Caleb Johnson (review): Rate limiter defaults: 2k/s seems high for prod; can we start lower for canary and ramp?

Thomas Baird (author): Yep—updated rollout notes: start canary at 500/s. Defaults in this PR are staging-oriented; prod defaults will be set in PR-18429 via environment config.

Final approvals:
- Logan Wright: Approved
- Nadia Rahman: Approved
- Omar El-Sayed: Approved
- Marcus Reed: Approved (perf note acknowledged)

Merge: Squash merged after CI green. Post-merge note: please coordinate with Allison/SRE before enabling in prod so dashboards include drop counters and we don’t misread throttled telemetry as a cache regression.
